Regional Emergency Department - Physician Record
Date of service: 4/18/2024
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

CC: tired, puffy face, dark urine.

HPI: 29F with SLE and class IV lupus nephritis (2022), on mycophenolate, prednisone 20 and lisinopril. Says this feels like the kidney flare in December 2022. Months of aching in hands and wrists, mouth sores coming and going recently. For about a week her eyelids are swollen on waking and her urine looks darker.

Exam: BP 150/95. Periorbital edema. Mild pitting edema both legs. Heart and lungs normal.

Results: creatinine 1.8. UA 2+ protein, numerous RBC casts. ANA positive. Anti-dsDNA positive. C3 low.

Impression: Lupus nephritis flare.

Plan: Discussed with her nephrologist's on-call partner. Prednisone increased to 40 mg daily for 4 weeks, then back to 20 mg. Continue mycophenolate and lisinopril. Nephrology clinic within 2 weeks; PCP this week. Return for low urine output, breathlessness, chest pain.

documents.title: Post-ED visit - nephritis flare
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED 4/18 for flare of lupus nephritis: Cr 1.8, 2+ protein, RBC casts, low C3. Prednisone up to 40 for four weeks.
Today: eyelid puffiness better, a little ankle swelling. Mouth sores healing. Hand and wrist aches persist. Says she has been taking the mycophenolate; a shipment came late in March and she may have gone a few days without.
Exam: mild periorbital fullness, trace ankle edema. Mouth sores healing. No synovitis. Lungs clear.
A/P: lupus nephritis flare - on prednisone 40 x4 wk per ED/nephrology, nephrology appt 4/30. Labs at that visit. Asked the coordinator to call the program about the shipping gap. HTN - running higher with the flare, recheck after taper. Epilepsy - stable.

Outside Nephrology - Follow-up
Date of service: 4/30/2024

Renal flare of class IV lupus nephritis, presented to ED 4/18 with creatinine 1.8, 2+ proteinuria, red cell casts, positive anti-dsDNA and low C3. Prednisone increased to 40 mg daily on 4/18.

Reports a short gap in mycophenolate in March. Now taking it reliably. Edema lessening.

Plan: Continue mycophenolate 1 g bid. Prednisone 40 mg daily through 5/16, then 20 mg daily. Lisinopril 10 mg. Labs in 6-8 weeks via PCP. Repeat biopsy not planned unless response is poor. Return in 6 months.

documents.author: critical care

Regional Hospital - Medical ICU Discharge Summary
Admitted 8/18/2024, discharged 8/22/2024
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

Admitting diagnosis: Refractory status epilepticus.

History: 30-year-old woman with SLE, class IV lupus nephritis (flare April 2024), and epilepsy, with an episode of generalized convulsive status one year ago. Brought by ambulance after recurrent seizures at home. Husband reports she has not been taking her medicines reliably for about a month. Paramedics gave lorazepam 4 mg IV en route; she arrived unresponsive. A second lorazepam dose was given and she was intubated for airway protection. Thirty minutes later her level of consciousness had not improved, without visible convulsive activity.

Exam: T 37.2 C, BP 130/85, pulse 88, RR 16 (ventilated). Postictal; no focal neurological deficit identified. Glucose 98.

Course: IV levetiracetam load and maintenance. Continuous EEG showed no ongoing electrographic seizures. Sedation lifted and extubated on hospital day 2. Mental status back to baseline. Renal function and urine monitored and stable during stay. Home mycophenolate, prednisone and lisinopril resumed.

Discharge medications: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily; mycophenolate mofetil 1000 mg twice daily; prednisone 20 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; fluticasone inhaler; albuterol as needed.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; neurology clinic. No driving for 6 months.

documents.title: Post-discharge visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharge summary 8/18-8/22 reviewed: refractory status, intubated, extubated day 2, EEG without ongoing seizures.

With husband today. Feels back to herself. She is quiet about the month before - work hours went up, she stopped filling the pill box, lost track of all of it. No intent to stop. No low mood on PHQ-2 screen.

Exam: alert, fluent, normal gait and strength. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. Status epilepticus, resolved. LEV 500 BID unchanged per hospital and neurology. Husband fills the pill box Sunday nights; pharmacy blister packs set up today. No driving 6 months.
2. Lupus nephritis - recheck labs at nephrology in October.
3. HTN, asthma - stable.
RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner anything.

Plan: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily unchanged. Reinforced that missed doses are the main risk. No driving until 2/2025. Return 1 year.

documents.body:
Annual. A hard year - kidney flare in April, ICU in August. No seizures since; blister packs working. Husband drives her for now. Feels okay. Tired after shifts. Sleep ok.
ROS: no edema, no joint swelling, no rash, no chest pain, no dyspnea.
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft. No edema. Joints normal. Neuro normal.
PHQ-9 5 - mild, situational; she declined counseling, knows how to reach us.
A/P: well visit. Lipids, CBC, CMP. Flu and COVID done in October. Pap next due 2026. Continue all medicines. RTC 3-4 months.

reports.text: Bedside limited transthoracic study. Bicuspid aortic valve. Aortic root dilated, 4.0 cm at the sinuses. Left ventricle normal in size with normal systolic function. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Bicuspid aortic valve with aortic root dilation (4.0 cm). Normal LV size and function.

reports.text: CT angiography of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. Dissection flap begins just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery and extends through the descending thoracic aorta. Ascending aorta and arch not involved. Celiac, superior mesenteric and both renal arteries arise from the true lumen and enhance normally. No periaortic hematoma or extravasation. Aortic root dilated, as on echocardiogram. Lungs clear.
reports.conclusion: Acute type B aortic dissection of the descending thoracic aorta, without malperfusion or rupture.

Regional Emergency Department - Physician Record
Date of service: 2/23/2025
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

CC: sudden tearing chest pain into the back.

HPI: 30-year-old woman with SLE, class IV lupus nephritis and prior status epilepticus. Abrupt severe tearing pain in the chest going through to the back, began several hours before arrival. Amenorrheic for years; has never been pregnant. On lisinopril for blood pressure.

Exam: BP 150/90 right arm, 140/85 left arm. Short stature (5 ft). Webbed neck, low posterior hairline. Diastolic murmur on auscultation. Lungs clear. Pulses present in all four limbs.

Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 7.2, platelets 250, creatinine 0.9.

Imaging: bedside echo - bicuspid aortic valve, dilated aortic root. CT angiography - type B dissection beginning beyond the left subclavian, descending thoracic aorta, no malperfusion.

Course: analgesia given; IV beta-blocker infusion begun for heart rate and pressure control. Vascular surgery consulted at bedside: medical management.

Disposition: admitted to cardiac ICU.

Regional Hospital - Vascular Surgery Discharge Summary
Admitted 2/23/2025, discharged 3/1/2025
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

Diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection. Bicuspid aortic valve with aortic root dilation (4.0 cm).

Course: Cardiac ICU for 3 days on IV beta-blockade with heart rate and pressure targets met; pain resolved by day 2. Transitioned to oral metoprolol succinate; home lisinopril continued. No malperfusion; renal function stable. Stepped down day 4, ambulating, discharged home.

Discharge medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (new); lisinopril 10 mg daily; mycophenolate 1000 mg bid; prednisone 20 mg daily; levetiracetam 500 mg bid; fluticasone; albuterol prn.

Follow-up: PCP 1 week; vascular surgery with CT angiography in 3 months; cardiology for bicuspid valve and root. Avoid heavy lifting and straining. Home BP goal under 120/80.

reports.text: Thin acute right convexity subdural hematoma. No significant midline shift. Basal cisterns patent. No skull fracture. Frontal scalp soft-tissue swelling.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Trauma protocol CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast. No solid organ injury. No free fluid or free air. No fractures. Lungs clear, no pneumothorax. Chronic type B dissection of the descending thoracic aorta, unchanged from 5/28/2025, without new injury.
reports.conclusion: No acute traumatic injury. Known type B dissection unchanged.

reports.text: Repeat after neurological decline. Interval enlargement of the acute right convexity subdural hematoma with 8 mm leftward midline shift and effacement of the right ambient cistern, consistent with early right uncal herniation.
reports.conclusion: Enlarging right subdural hematoma with 8 mm midline shift and early uncal herniation.

documents.title: Trauma Bay Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional Trauma Center - Emergency Physician Record
Date of service: 12/29/2025
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics

31-year-old woman, restrained driver, head-on collision. History of SLE with lupus nephritis, two episodes of status epilepticus and a type B aortic dissection (2/2025).

Arrival: agitated but alert, GCS 14. BP 130/85, HR 92, RR 22, SpO2 98% room air. Repeat BP 155/90, HR 88, RR 18.

Survey: forehead contusion; no other obvious injury. Pupils equal and reactive, right slightly sluggish. FAST negative.

About two hours after arrival, increasingly drowsy and complaining of right-sided headache. Non-contrast head CT: small right subdural hematoma without significant midline shift. Trauma CT body: no acute injury; known dissection unchanged.

Neurosurgery at bedside; admitted to neuro ICU.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Regional Trauma Center - Neurosurgery Operative Report
Date of surgery: 12/29/2025

Preoperative diagnosis: acute right subdural hematoma with midline shift and early uncal herniation.
Procedure: emergency right frontotemporoparietal craniotomy and evacuation of subdural hematoma.

Indication: further decline in level of consciousness; repeat CT with enlargement, 8 mm shift and early uncal herniation.

Findings: acute subdural clot over the right convexity, evacuated. Bone flap replaced. Subdural drain placed.

EBL modest. No complications. To neuro ICU intubated.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Regional Trauma Center - Neurosurgery Discharge Summary
Admitted 12/29/2025, discharged 1/9/2026

Diagnoses: traumatic acute right subdural hematoma with brain herniation, status post right craniotomy and evacuation 12/29/2025. Forehead contusion.

Course: emergency evacuation the night of admission. Extubated postoperative day 1. Drain removed day 2. Postop CT satisfactory. Levetiracetam continued at home dose without seizures. Blood pressure held within dissection goals on home metoprolol and lisinopril. Prednisone and mycophenolate continued. Mental status returned to baseline; no focal deficits. Worked with PT/OT, cleared for home with husband.

Discharge medications: unchanged from admission (levetiracetam 500 mg bid; metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily; mycophenolate 1000 mg bid; prednisone 20 mg daily; fluticasone; albuterol prn).

Follow-up: neurosurgery 4-6 weeks with CT head. PCP 1 week. Staples out at PCP day 10-14. No driving until cleared by neurosurgery and neurology.
